title: The Burnout Reset
subtitle: Recognise it, name it, recover from it
description: You are 18 months into a demanding role. The symptoms are obvious to everyone except you — until one Thursday morning when you cannot get out of bed. This is the story of what happens next.
learning_objectives: Recognise early warning signs of burnout before crisis point
Identify sustainable work interventions that do not require quitting
Build a personal recovery plan that addresses root causes
reflection_prompt: What is one signal from this story that you have noticed in yourself recently, and what would you do about it?

scenes.title: Thursday Morning
scenes.narration: It is 8:14 am. You are still in bed. Your phone has 22 unread Slack messages and a missed call from your manager. Your head feels like concrete. You realise with a slow shock: you cannot make yourself move. This has been building for months. You have three calls today.

choices.label: Push through — message everyone you will be online in 20 minutes
Message your manager: 'I am not okay. I need today off.'
Sit with it for an hour before deciding anything

scenes.narration: You get through the day on adrenaline. By 7pm you are lying on the floor next to your desk, phone face-down. Your body forced the break your mind would not take. Your partner asks if you are okay. You say 'fine.'

choices.label: Tell your partner the truth — you are not fine
Go to sleep and hope tomorrow is better

scenes.narration: Your manager replies within five minutes: 'Please rest. Let us talk tomorrow about what support you need.' You exhale for the first time in weeks. The day without notifications feels strange — then slowly, like a window opening.

choices.label: Use the day to think about what you actually need
Spend the day catching up on email anyway

scenes.narration: In that hour of silence you notice: your shoulders are permanently tense, you have not cooked a meal in three weeks, and you cannot remember your last real day off. By 9am you know what you need to do.

choices.label: Block your calendar for the rest of the week and tell your manager you need a reset
Go in but cancel the afternoon meetings only

scenes.narration: You spend three days offline. You sleep. You walk. You write down everything that has been consuming you. When you return you have a short list: three structural changes that would make the job sustainable. Your manager agrees to two of them in the first conversation.
scenes.outcome_summary: Recovery is not a weakness break — it is diagnostic work. You came back with information, not just rest.

scenes.narration: Your partner helps you see the pattern you have been inside. Together you identify two things you can stop doing immediately. The next week is still hard, but for the first time in months you feel like you have agency over it.
scenes.outcome_summary: Sometimes recovery starts with one honest conversation with someone who is not at work.

scenes.narration: The half-measure helps a little. The root causes remain. Two weeks later you are back in the same place — but now you have more information about where the boundaries actually need to go.
scenes.outcome_summary: Partial interventions are not failure — they are data. You now know that half-measures are not enough.

scenes.narration: Three more weeks pass. The crash is worse when it comes. But you notice it sooner this time. Awareness, even delayed, is progress.
scenes.outcome_summary: You cannot skip the hard parts, but you can get faster at recognising them. That is how resilience actually works.
